question: In how many of the 12 settings do agents beat the strongest human-engineered SSL baselines, and by up to how much?

results.text: We find that even under weak feedback and matched compute, agents can synthesize code that combines and adapts established SSL techniques, exceeding the strongest human-engineered baselines in 8 of 12 settings by up to +21.8%.

9 Discussion and Conclusion

We introduced AgentSSL, which formulates semi-supervised learning as agentic program search. Under label scarcity, MLE agents generate SSL programs that beat tuned human baselines in 8 of 12 settings when the best program is known, but neither agents nor human pipelines can reliably pick that program without labels.

Indeed, prior work has shown that, in many settings, well-tuned SL can perform comparably to state-of-the-art SSL methods [39]. To investigate this relationship in the context of AgentSSL, we conduct an ablation in which agents are not given access to unlabeled data.

6.3 Do Agents Adapt SSL to Different Domains Effectively?

One benefit of AgentSSL is the ability to discover dataset-specific learning strategies rather than relying on a single fixed SSL recipe. Figure 5 shows that programs discovered for one dataset often transfer poorly to others i.e., the strongest programs are adapted to their source domain.

question: What does oracle performance measure when assessing program discovery?

results.text: Evaluation. We evaluate these two challenges separately. To assess program discovery, we measure oracle performance, defined as the test performance of the best program in the discovered pool, Q(A∗). This measures the quality of the best discovered solution, independent of our ability to select it.

When the metric is well correlated with test performance, much of the oracle performance is retained; when this alignment is weak, selection performance can degrade substantially. These results suggest that practical program selection is a major bottleneck for AgentSSL.

The gap between oracle and practical selection, however, highlights a central challenge for AgentSSL and SSL more broadly:identifying the best discovered program when validation feedback is weak. Table 2 reports practical selection regret when using the feedback metric for selection.
